newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GEC shifts focus from joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GEC shifts focus from joint ventures.

text.p: British engineering giant General Electric Co Plc unveiled on Tuesday the strategic blueprint to take it into the next century, marking a move away from joint ventures to form a world force in defence, aerospace, industrial electronics and communications.
GEC-Marconi, the defence division, will become the new heart of the group, said George Simpson, GEC's managing director and successor to the former veteran chief Lord Weinstock.

"The ambitious repositioning strategy announced today is designed to build Marconi into a global player, spanning all three principle defence electronics markets -- America, Europe and the East -- and to focus the group's industrial electronics and communications activities on existing or potential global leadership positions," said Simpson, summing up the new mission statement.

GEC said the future of its two major joint ventures was up for review. The British group said it was in "active discussions" with French partner Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' over the future of the 50-50 rail and power venture GEC-ALSTHOM.
It is also considering "repositioning" the telecoms venture GPT which is 60 percent owned by GEC and 40 percent owned by Germany's Siemens AG.
The first call on GEC's one billion pounds-plus ($1.7 billion) cash mountain will be investment and acquisition opportunities to grow the chosen core sectors.
But there was no concrete news on acquisition plans or
mention of merger talks, as speculated earlier this week. GEC shares fell after the announcement on what traders said was a lack of tangible news, trading down 5-1/2 pence at 372.
"The investment required to fulfill this growth strategy -- both product development expenditure and acquisitions -- will be financed from GEC's substantial cash resources," said Simpson.
That cash will grow further once more divestments of non-core businesses are completed.
But Simpson said surplus cash after these deals could possibly be returned to shareholders. "Any surplus cash will be remitted to shareholders."
The news marks a radical shake-up at the group which has been seen to be drifting in a state of strategic slumber in recent years.

Under Lord Weinstock's final years of tenure as managing director many market analysts had been critical of GEC's inability to use its financial muscle to clinch deals to consolidate its global position.

The shake-up comes against a backdrop of mounting pressure for the European defence industry to consolidate after mega-mergers in the U.S. between Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp plus Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas
Analysts had hoped that last week's shock departure of finance director David Newlands signalled a changing of the guard to free Simpson's hands to pursue a major merger or takeover.
Newlands exit led to a resurgence of the old rumours of a merger between GEC and British Aerospace
Separately, last night GEC damped press speculation that it may merge its defence interests with Italy's Finmeccanica SpA.

In a statement, GEC had said talks continued "successfully" between the two but "both companies wish to make it clear that this co-operation does not involve either company acquiring the other's defence interests."
Turning to GEC's annual results, the comapny said pretax profits were 707 million pounds after taking a 303 million pounds charge, mostly related to restructuring.
Before the charge, profits were in line with forecasts at 1.01 billion pounds versus 981 million the previous year.
The total dividend was 13.15 pence per share. The defence business GEC-Marconi showed strong profits growth in particular, rising 18.6 percent. Orders were up 40 percent.
But the strong pound took a 19 million pounds bite out of profits and damped back sales, said GEC.
